svg.title: Neuropathic pain has a neurological cause and is recognized by its descriptors; after the cause is evaluated, one agent is chosen by the co-existing problem (amitriptyline for poor sleep or low cost, duloxetine for depression, carbamazepine for trigeminal neuralgia, gabapentinoids, topicals) with narcotics only as a last resort, and titrated by trial and error

svg.text: NEUROPATHIC pain: a neurological cause, peripheral or central

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: sounds like: electrical · shooting · burning, hot or cold · pins and needles

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: allodynia: a non-painful touch hurts · hyperpathia: a painful stimulus hurts far too much · dysesthesia: uncomfortable

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: peripheral causes: length-dependent (diabetic, small fibre, chemotherapy) · radiculopathy · postherpetic neuralgia · trigeminal

svg.text: central causes: thalamus · brainstem · spinal cord · phantom limb pain partly central

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: EVALUATE THE CAUSE and examine: an important neurological diagnosis? some are reversible · nociceptive pain (tissue
